claim: The N-terminal portion of HIP1 (residues 1-363) bound to Ub in a Y2H screening method called 'DEEPN'
source: In a previous study that used a large-scale Y2H screening method referred to as 'DEEPN', we found that the N-terminal portion of HIP1 bound to Ub (Pashkova et al., 2016). This Y2H interaction was observed between a Gal4-DNA-binding domain fused to two tandem copies of Ub linked via a three residue spacer and a the Gal4-transcriptional activation domain fused to residues 1–363 of mouse HIP1 (XP_036020882).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Pashkova et al., 2016) and described experimental observation

claim: GST-fused residues 1-363 of mouse HIP1 bound K63-linked polyubiquitin chains
source: This interaction was further validated by pulldown of GST-fused to residues 1–363 of mouse HIP1, which bound K63-linked polyubiquitin chains (Pashkova et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Pashkova et al., 2016) describing pulldown experiments

claim: The N-terminal fragment of HIP1 (residues 1-363) contains the ANTH domain
source: This fragment contains the ANTH (AP180 N-Terminal Homology) domain and indicated that the N-terminal ANTH domain of HIP1 might be an unrecognized Ub-binding domain (Figure 1).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1 domain organization diagram

claim: The ANTH domain alone from HIP1 is sufficient for Ub-binding
source: GST-pulldown experiments with the ANTH domain alone from HIP1 confirmed this was sufficient for Ub-binding (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C

claim: ANTH domains are part of the larger family of ENTH and VHS domains
source: ANTH domains are part of the larger family of ENTH (Epsin N-Terminal Homology) and VHS (Vps27, HRS, STAM) domains that are found in the N-terminus of proteins that play a variety of roles in endocytosis and many bind Ub (Figure 1A; Moshkanbaryans et al., 2014; Takatori and Tomita, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work (Moshkanbaryans et al., 2014; Takatori and Tomita, 2019) and established knowledge

claim: ANTH domains are structurally similar to ENTH domains but are larger, with an additional 3 C-terminal α-helices
source: ANTH domains are structurally similar to ENTH domains but are larger, with an additional 3 C-terminal α-helices.
evidence: Stated as established structural knowledge

claim: There are two broad subgroups of ANTH domains by sequence homology: those found in CALM and AP180, and those found in HIP1, HIP1R, and Sla2
source: By sequence homology, there are two broad subgroups of ANTH domains, those found in proteins such as CALM and AP180 and those found in HIP1, HIP1R, and Sla2 (De Craene et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (De Craene et al., 2012)

claim: Multiple ANTH domains from both subcategories bind Ub in solution with equilibrium binding constants ranging from 2.9 ± 0.4 µM to 33 ± 6 µM
source: Binding in solution was monitored by HSQC NMR of 15N-Ub in increasing concentrations of ANTH domains. This produced both chemical shift perturbations as well as overall peak broadening, indicating binding was in fast-exchange. Binding of Ub to 15N-labeled HIP1-ANTH was also observed in HSQC experiments, which produced selective chemical shift perturbations in backbone amides of 15N-HIP1 ANTH as well (Figure 1—figure supplement 1). These concentration dependent changes allowed us to derive equilibrium binding constants for each ANTH domain, ranging from 2.9 ± 0.4 µM for the mouse HIP1 ANTH domain to 33 ± 6 µM for Drosophila LAP, a homolog of human AP180.
evidence: Supported by NMR experimental data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: All ANTH domains tested bound a similar surface on Ub centered on L8, I44, and V70
source: Mapping the largest backbone amide chemical shift perturbations in 15N-Ub (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) onto the structure of Ub (Figure 1D) indicated that all ANTH domains bound a similar surface on Ub centered on L8, I44, and V70, which mediates the vast majority of Ub-binding interactions (Piper et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by NMR data analysis shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1, with citation to previous work (Piper et al., 2014)

claim: A crystal structure of the human CALM ANTH domain in complex with Ub was resolved to 2.4 Å
source: To gain further insight into how ANTH domains bound Ub, we obtained a crystal structure of the human CALM ANTH domain in a complex with Ub resolved to 2.4 Å (Figure 2, Table 1, PDB:7JXV).
evidence: Supported by crystallographic data shown in Figure 2 and Table 1

claim: Ub binds near a loop within the C-terminal three-helical portion of the CALM ANTH domain connecting the last two α-helices
source: These data showed that Ub bound near a loop within the C-terminal three-helical portion of the ANTH domain connecting the last two α-helices (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by crystal structure data shown in Figure 2A

claim: The structure of CALM when bound to Ub had extensive overlap with a previously determined crystal structure of CALM alone (PDB:1HFA), indicating that the CALM-ANTH does not undergo large conformational rearrangements upon binding Ub
source: The structure of CALM when bound to Ub had extensive overlap with a previously determined crystal structure of CALM alone (PDB:1HFA) (Ford et al., 2001), indicating that the CALM-ANTH does not undergo large conformational rearrangements upon binding Ub (Figure 2B).
evidence: Supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 2B and citation to previous work (Ford et al., 2001)

claim: NMR experiments with 15N-labeled HIP1 ANTH domain showed that the HSQC spectra is largely unaltered upon Ub-binding
source: This result is also consistent with NMR experiments with 15N-labeled HIP1 ANTH domain showing that the HSQC spectra is largely unaltered upon Ub-binding (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by NMR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B

claim: The CALM-ANTH:Ub interface shows hydrophobic interactions between Ub (L8, I44, V70) and CALM ANTH (F223, L274)
source: The CALM-ANTH:Ub interface showed hydrophobic interactions between Ub (L8, I44, V70) and CALM ANTH (F223, L274); and electrostatic interactions between Ub (R42, K48) and CALM (D224, D276)
evidence: Supported by crystal structure analysis

claim: The CALM-ANTH:Ub interface shows electrostatic interactions between Ub (R42, K48) and CALM (D224, D276)
source: The CALM-ANTH:Ub interface showed hydrophobic interactions between Ub (L8, I44, V70) and CALM ANTH (F223, L274); and electrostatic interactions between Ub (R42, K48) and CALM (D224, D276)
evidence: Supported by crystal structure analysis

claim: PRE effects from HSQC of 15N-Ub resulting from binding to CALM spin-labeled at residues 209, 268, and 284 confirmed that in solution, Ub bound the same region and orientation as observed in the crystal structure
source: The largest PRE effects from the HSQC of 15N-Ub resulting from binding to CALM spin-labeled at residues 209, 268, and 284 were mapped onto the CALM:Ub structure and confirmed that in solution, Ub bound the same region and orientation as observed in the crystal structure.
evidence: Supported by PRE NMR experiments described in text and shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: Mutation of F223 to Ser or Ala in CALM ANTH abolished detectable Ub-binding in HSQC experiments
source: Although wildtype CALM-ANTH caused significant chemical shift perturbations within the 15N HSQC spectra, no perturbations were observed when F223 was altered to Ser or Ala alone or in combination with altering D224R or D276A (Figure 3A).
evidence: Supported by NMR data shown in Figure 3A

claim: The double mutant L274A, D276A in CALM ANTH abolished detectable Ub-binding in HSQC experiments
source: Likewise, no Ub-binding was observed by the double mutant L274A, D276A.
evidence: Supported by NMR experiments described in text

claim: GST-pulldown experiments confirmed that CALM ANTH carrying the F223A single substitution or the combined F223S and D224R double substitutions did not bind GST fused to five tandem copies of linear Ub
source: These results were confirmed in GST-pulldown experiments using GST fused to five tandem copies of linear Ub (Figure 3C) that bound the wildtype CALM ANTH domain but not a mutant ANTH domain carrying the F223A single substitution or the combined F223S and D224R double substitutions.
evidence: Supported by GST-pulldown data shown in Figure 3C

claim: The region of CALM responsible for Ub-binding is highly conserved across a subgroup of ANTH domains that includes Drosophila melanogaster LAP and Saccharomyces cerevisiae Yap1801 and Yap1802
source: This region of CALM is highly conserved across a subgroup of ANTH domains that includes Drosophila melanogaster LAP and Saccharomyces cerevisiae Yap1801 and Yap1802.
evidence: Stated based on sequence analysis

claim: Mutation of residues F238 and D239 in Drosophila LAP (corresponding to F223 and D224 in rat CALM) ablated detectable binding to 15N-Ub as monitored with HSQC experiments
source: Accordingly, mutation of residues F238 and D239 in LAP, which correspond to F223 and D224 in rat CALM, ablated detectable binding to 15N-Ub as monitored with HSQC experiments (Figure 4).
evidence: Supported by NMR data shown in Figure 4

claim: The CALM ANTH domain was shown previously to bind endocytic SNAREs VAMP7 and VAMP8
source: The CALM ANTH domain was shown previously to bind endocytic SNAREs VAMP7 and VAMP8, which is a property conserved by the S. cerevisiae orthologs of CALM, Yap1801, and Yap1802 (Burston et al., 2009; Fujimoto et al., 2020; Koo et al., 2011; Miller et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work (Burston et al., 2009; Fujimoto et al., 2020; Koo et al., 2011; Miller et al., 2011)

claim: CALM should not be able to bind simultaneously to v-SNAREs and Ub because the binding sites substantially overlap
source: This proposed binding mode for v-SNAREs substantially overlaps with that for Ub. Moreover, the binding site for Ub relies on the position of the last helical region of the ANTH domain, whereas this region would have to be dramatically repositioned to allow v-SNARE binding at the site it occupies in the crystal structure (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A). Thus, CALM should not be able to bind simultaneously to v-SNAREs and Ub.
evidence: Supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A

claim: Wildtype CALM ANTH domain as well as ANTH domain containing the F223A mutation or the F223S, D224R double mutation all bound GST-VAMP7
source: Therefore, we performed binding experiments using GST-VAMP7 (Figure 3C). Wildtype ANTH domain as well as ANTH domain containing the F223A mutation or the F223S, D224R double mutation all bound GST-VAMP7.
evidence: Supported by GST-pulldown data shown in Figure 3C

claim: Inclusion of excess free linear Ub chains diminished binding of wildtype CALM ANTH domain on GST-VAMP7 indicating that Ub and VAMP7 binding are mutually exclusive
source: Additionally, inclusion of excess free linear Ub (5 x) chains diminished binding of wildtype ANTH domain on GST-VAMP7 indicating that Ub and VAMP7 binding are mutually exclusive.
evidence: Supported by GST-pulldown experiments described in text and shown in Figure 3C

claim: Inclusion of 5 x linear Ub chains had no effect on the ability of VAMP7 to bind to the mutant CALM ANTH domains that lacked their Ub-binding sites
source: In contrast, inclusion of 5 x linear Ub chains had no effect on the ability VAMP7 to bind to the mutant ANTH domains that lacked their Ub-binding sites.
evidence: Supported by GST-pulldown experiments described in text

claim: The F223A/S, D224R mutations in CALM ANTH specifically ablate Ub-binding but not v-SNARE binding
source: These results show that the F223A/S, D224R mutations specifically ablate Ub-binding but not v-SNARE binding.
evidence: Supported by GST-pulldown experiments described in text and shown in Figure 3C

claim: Mutations L219S and M244K in CALM ANTH abolished all detectable Ub-binding in NMR HSQC experiments with 15N-Ub
source: Previous studies also identified mutations (L219S and M244K) that ablated binding of CALM to v-SNAREs. However, these mutations also abolished all detectable Ub-binding in NMR HSQC experiments with 15N-Ub (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by NMR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B

claim: Recombinant C. thermophilum Sla2 ANTH domain had negligible binding to Ub
source: We found that recombinant C. thermophilum Sla2 ANTH domain had negligible binding to Ub, preventing a structural analysis of Ub-binding by this ANTH domain (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by NMR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2

claim: Spin-labels placed in the N-terminal portion of the Sla2 ANTH domain did not yield PRE effects
source: Spin-labels placed in the N-terminal portion of the Sla2 ANTH domain did not yield PRE effects (Figure 4B, left) despite comparable binding overall to Ub (Figure 4B, middle).
evidence: Supported by PRE NMR data shown in Figure 4B

claim: Spin labels in the C-terminal portion of the Sla2 ANTH domain near the presumptive Ub-binding site gave strong PRE effects
source: In contrast, spin labels in the C-terminal portion of the Sla2 ANTH domain that were near the presumptive Ub-binding site predicated by structure and sequence homology (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-C) gave strong PRE effects (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by PRE NMR data shown in Figure 4B and structural models in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-C

claim: GST fused to the HIP1 or Sla2 ANTH domain bound K63 linked polyubiquitin chains well
source: GST-pulldown assays showed that these residues were indeed required for efficient binding of Ub. GST fused to the HIP1 or Sla2 ANTH domain bound K63 linked polyubiquitin chains well (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by GST-pulldown data shown in Figure 4C

claim: Altering L250 or D253 to arginines in mouse HIP1 ablated detectable binding to K63 linked polyubiquitin chains
source: Altering L250 or D253 to arginines in mouse HIP1 or L212 and D218 to alanines in Sla2 ablated detectable binding.
evidence: Supported by GST-pulldown experiments described in text and shown in Figure 4C

claim: Altering L212 and D218 to alanines in Sla2 ablated detectable binding to K63 linked polyubiquitin chains
source: Altering L250 or D253 to arginines in mouse HIP1 or L212 and D218 to alanines in Sla2 ablated detectable binding.
evidence: Supported by GST-pulldown experiments described in text and shown in Figure 4C

claim: The human HIP1 L250S, D253R double mutant failed to bind di-Ub via a yeast two-hybrid assay
source: Similarly, the human HIP1 L250S, D253R double mutant or the hHIP1R L241S, D244R double mutant failed to bind di-Ub via a yeast two-hybrid assay, in contrast to the robust interaction observed with wildtype human HIP1 and human HIP1R ANTH domains (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: Supported by yeast two-hybrid data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D, E

claim: The hHIP1R L241S, D244R double mutant failed to bind di-Ub via a yeast two-hybrid assay
source: Similarly, the human HIP1 L250S, D253R double mutant or the hHIP1R L241S, D244R double mutant failed to bind di-Ub via a yeast two-hybrid assay, in contrast to the robust interaction observed with wildtype human HIP1 and human HIP1R ANTH domains (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: Supported by yeast two-hybrid data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D, E

claim: NMR titrations with mutant L212A, D218A Sla2 ANTH domain showed a > 10 fold loss of apparent Kd for Ub-binding in comparison with wildtype Sla2 ANTH domain
source: NMR titrations with mutant L212A, D218A Sla2 ANTH domain showed a > 10 fold loss of apparent Kd for Ub-binding in comparison with wildtype Sla2 ANTH domain (Figure 4D).
evidence: Supported by NMR titration data shown in Figure 4D

claim: Even less binding was observed in HSQC experiments when Sla2 ANTH carried an L212S, D218R double mutation
source: Even less binding was observed in HSQC experiments when Sla2 ANTH carried an L212S, D218R double mutation (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by NMR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2

claim: Sla2 plays a major role in internalization in yeast and its loss causes severe defects in the internalization of proteins and lipid dyes
source: Sla2 plays a major role in internalization in yeast and its loss causes severe defects in the internalization of proteins and lipid dyes and disrupts the ordered assembly of the endocytic apparatus and transition to actin polymerization (Brach et al., 2014; Kaksonen et al., 2003; Newpher et al., 2005; Skruzny et al., 2015; Wesp et al., 1997).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work (Brach et al., 2014; Kaksonen et al., 2003; Newpher et al., 2005; Skruzny et al., 2015; Wesp et al., 1997)

claim: Sla2 forms a complex with Ent1/2 (yeast Epsins) that can bridge PtdIns(4,5)P2-containing membranes with the actin cytoskeleton via its PtdIns(4,5)P2-binding ANTH domain and C-terminal THATCH domains
source: Sla2 forms a complex with Ent1/2 (yeast Epsins) that can bridge PtdIns(4,5)P2-containing membranes with the actin cytoskeleton via its PtdIns(4,5)P2-binding ANTH domain and C-terminal THATCH domains, respectively (Skruzny et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Skruzny et al., 2015)

claim: Sla2 arrives early in the assembly process and remains during actin polymerization
source: Sla2 arrives early in the assembly process and remains during actin polymerization making it a plausible candidate cargo receptor.
evidence: Stated based on established knowledge of Sla2 function

claim: Yap1801 and Yap1802 localize with clathrin at the cell surface and arrive in the early phase of CME assembly
source: Both localize with clathrin at the cell surface and arrive in the early phase of CME assembly (Carroll et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Carroll et al., 2012)

claim: Loss of both Yap1801 and Yap1802 has no effect on GPCR internalization but does cause accumulation of the v-SNARE Snc1 at the cell surface
source: Loss of both has no effect on GPCR internalization but does cause accumulation of the v-SNARE Snc1 at the cell surface implying they work as dedicated cargo-specific adaptors for a subset of proteins (Burston et al., 2009; Huang et al., 1999; Maldonado-Báez et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work (Burston et al., 2009; Huang et al., 1999; Maldonado-Báez et al., 2008)

claim: Internalization of wildtype Ste2 was rapid and complete within 10 min
source: As expected, internalization of wildtype Ste2 was rapid and complete within 10 min (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: Supported by internalization assay data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, C

claim: Truncated Ste2 lacking its NPFxD-like motif yet still possessing ubiquitinatable lysines (Ste2-∆C) had an intermediate rate of internalization
source: In contrast, truncated Ste2 lacking its NPFxD-like motif yet still possessing ubiquitinatable lysines (Ste2-∆C), had an intermediate rate of internalization.
evidence: Supported by internalization assay data described in text and shown in Figure 5D

claim: Ste2 containing an intact NPFxD motif but carrying K > R mutations (Ste2-8K > R) within its cytosolic domain internalized at an intermediate rate, though somewhat slower than the truncated Ste2
source: Likewise, Ste2 containing an intact NPFxD motif but carrying K > R mutations (Ste2-8K > R) within its cytosolic domain also internalized at an intermediate rate, though somewhat slower than the truncated Ste2.
evidence: Supported by internalization assay data described in text and shown in Figure 5D

claim: A truncated mutant Ste2 lacking its NPFxD motif and its C-terminal ubiquitinatable lysines (Ste2-∆C,8K > R) showed almost no internalization
source: In contrast, a truncated mutant Ste2 lacking its NPFxD motif and its C-terminal ubiquitinatable lysines (Ste2-∆C,8K > R) showed almost no internalization.
evidence: Supported by internalization assay data described in text and shown in Figure 5D

claim: When all Ub-binding mutations in Sla2, Yap1801, and Yap1802 were combined (3xANTH∆Ub), internalization of α-factorRhD uptake by Ste2 via its Ub-dependent (Ste2-∆C) or Ub-independent routes (Ste2-8K > R) was unaffected
source: When all these mutations were combined (3xANTH∆Ub), internalization assays showed that α-factorRhD uptake by Ste2 via its Ub-dependent (Ste2-∆C) (Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B-C) or Ub-independent routes (Ste2-8K > R) (Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, C) was unaffected.
evidence: Supported by internalization assay data shown in Figure 5E, 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B-C

claim: Combined loss of Ub-binding activity of Ent1/2 and Ede1 had no effect on α-factorRhD internalization
source: Combined loss of Ub-binding activity of Ent1/2 and Ede1 had no effect on α-factorRhD internalization (Figure 5E) in agreement with previous studies (Dores et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by internalization assay data shown in Figure 5E and citation to previous work (Dores et al., 2010)

claim: Loss of Ub-binding by Ede1 or loss of Ub-binding in both Ent1 and Ent2 had no affect on internalization when each was combined with loss of Ub-binding in all ANTH domains
source: Likewise, loss of Ub-binding by Ede1 or loss of Ub-binding in both Ent1 and Ent2 had no affect on internalization when each was combined with loss of Ub-binding in all ANTH domains.
evidence: Supported by internalization assay data described in text

claim: Marked reduction in α-factorRhD internalization by Ste2∆C was observed in strains carrying all mutations in which Ub-binding mutations in Ent1/2 and Ede1 were combined with Ub-binding mutations in all of the ANTH domain proteins, Sla2, Yap1801, and Yap1802
source: In contrast, marked reduction in α-factorRhD internalization by Ste2∆C was observed in strains carrying all of these mutations in which Ub-binding mutations in Ent1/2 and Ede1 were combined with Ub-binding mutations in all of the ANTH domain proteins, Sla2, Yap1801, and Yap1802 (Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by internalization assay data shown in Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C

claim: Combined loss of Ub-binding by the three ANTH domains in addition to Ent1/2 and Ede1 had no effect on α-factorRhD internalization by Ste2-8K > R, which has an NPFxD internalization motif
source: We also assessed the effect of these mutant combinations on the internalization of Ste2-8K > R, which has an NPFxD interanalization motif. Here, combined loss of Ub-binding by the three ANTH domains in addition to Ent1/2 and Ede1 had no effect on α-factorRhD internalization (Figure 5F).
evidence: Supported by internalization assay data shown in Figure 5F

claim: The combination of mutations that inactivated Ub-binding by a whole cohort of Ub-binding proteins was selective for a cargo that uses Ub as an internalization signal
source: Thus, the combination of mutations that inactivated Ub-binding by a whole cohort of Ub-binding proteins was selective for a cargo that uses Ub as an internalization signal, demonstrating that the general ability of cells to execute and regulate internalization was largely intact.
evidence: Supported by comparison of internalization data for Ste2-∆C vs Ste2-8K>R in mutant strains

claim: Ubiquitination of membrane proteins is a signal for internalization via clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME), a process largely conserved across eukaryotes
source: At the plasma membrane, ubiquitination of membrane proteins is a signal for internalization via clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME), a process largely conserved across eukaryotes (Kaksonen and Roux, 2018; Traub and Lukacs, 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work (Kaksonen and Roux, 2018; Traub and Lukacs, 2007)

claim: Ub is a versatile signal for internalization since it can be added or removed from virtually all membrane proteins by a myriad of regulatory mechanisms
source: Ub is a versatile signal for internalization since it can be added or removed from virtually all membrane proteins by a myriad of regulatory mechanisms (Traub, 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Traub, 2009)

claim: The fact that Ub can serve as an internalization signal has been clearly demonstrated with reporter membrane proteins translationally fused to Ub, which accelerates the rate of their internalization
source: The fact that Ub can serve as an internalization signal has been clearly demonstrated with reporter membrane proteins translationally fused to Ub, which accelerates the rate of their internalization (Traub and Lukacs, 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Traub and Lukacs, 2007)

claim: The first instance of Ub as an internalization signal was recognized in yeast where it controls the internalization of the GPCR Ste2 that can be followed by the uptake of its ligand α-factor
source: The first instance of Ub as an internalization signal was recognized in yeast where it controls the internalization of the GPCR Ste2 that can be followed by the uptake of its ligand α-factor (Hicke and Riezman, 1996).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Hicke and Riezman, 1996)

claim: Ste2 has other internalization signals that operate in tandem with Ub
source: Yet, Ste2 has other internalization signals that operate in tandem with Ub, likely reflecting the ability of this GPCR to be regulated at the level of internalization by multiple mechanisms (Howard et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Howard et al., 2002)

claim: EGFR uses multiple internalization signals besides Ub to access CME and also uses different internalization routes from the plasma membrane
source: Yet EGFR also uses multiple internalization signals besides Ub to access CME and also uses different internalization routes from the plasma membrane (Caldieri et al., 2017; Fortian et al., 2015; Goh et al., 2010; Pascolutti et al., 2019; Sigismund et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work (Caldieri et al., 2017; Fortian et al., 2015; Goh et al., 2010; Pascolutti et al., 2019; Sigismund et al., 2013)

claim: Among the best characterized candidates for cargo receptors for Ub are Ede1/Eps15 and Ent1, Ent2/Epsin, which harbor Ub-binding domains, associate with Ub-cargo, and help concentrate Ub-cargo in forming CME sites
source: Among the best characterized candidates are Ede1/Eps15 and Ent1, Ent2/Epsin, yeast, and human orthologs, respectively, which harbor Ub-binding domains, associate with Ub-cargo, and help concentrate Ub-cargo in forming CME sites (Traub, 2009; Traub and Lukacs, 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work (Traub, 2009; Traub and Lukacs, 2007)

claim: Combined inactivation of Ub-binding domains within Ent1/2 and Ede1 in yeast does not affect Ub-dependent internalization of the Ste2 GPCR
source: Yet, the model that these components function as the sole adaptors for Ub-cargo does not represent the whole story since combined inactivation of Ub-binding domains within these proteins (eg. Ent1/2 and Ede1) in yeast does not affect Ub-dependent internalization of the Ste2 GPCR, suggesting other components help recognize Ub-internalization signals (Dores et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Dores et al., 2010)

claim: Ub binds with µM affinity to a unique C-terminal region within the ANTH domain not found in ENTH domains
source: Structural studies revealed that Ub binds with µM affinity to a unique C-terminal region within the ANTH domain not found in ENTH domains.
evidence: Supported by structural and NMR data presented in the manuscript

claim: Combined loss of Ub-binding by ANTH-domain proteins and other Ub-binding domains within the yeast internalization apparatus caused defects in the Ub-dependent internalization of the GPCR Ste2 that was engineered to rely exclusively on Ub as an internalization signal
source: Functional studies showed that combined loss of Ub-binding by ANTH-domain proteins and other Ub-binding domains within the yeast internalization apparatus caused defects in the Ub-dependent internalization of the GPCR Ste2 that was engineered to rely exclusively on Ub as an internalization signal.
evidence: Supported by internalization assay data presented in the manuscript

claim: Mutations that ablated Ub-binding had no effect on the internalization of Ste2 engineered to use an alternate Ub-independent internalization signal
source: In contrast, these mutations had no effect on the internalization of Ste2 engineered to use an alternate Ub-independent internalization signal.
evidence: Supported by internalization assay data presented in the manuscript
